_readme: Seedance 2.0: the earlier clip model, the sibling of seedance-2.5.json (Higgsfield API; BytePlus ModelArk is the maker's own door). Filled 2026-10-28 from BytePlus's Seedance 2.0 series tutorial and prompt guide, in the same shape as seedance-2.5.json so one library, one slice renderer and one checker serve both.
The 2.0 series is three models: standard (dreamina-seedance-2-0-260128), fast and mini. This sheet is the standard model. Fast and mini take the same inputs but output 480p or 720p only.

Anything marked UNCONFIRMED came only from a reseller's page or could not be read on the maker's own page; check it before a chain depends on it. Every row carries its source; every entry is status draft until it is approved. No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
Not yet in the Model House: no job names registry id seedance-2.0, so for_job() never reaches this sheet. A chain can load('seedance-2.0') by name until a row is added.
label: Seedance 2.0

limits.aspect_ratios: 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 or adaptive (a fixed list, not 2.5's free 0.4 to 2.5 range)
limits.real_faces_blocked: reference pictures or videos with a real human face are refused by the maker's moderation unless they are the account's own model outputs, the maker's preset characters or authorized portrait assets

house.duration: 4 to 15 s, the model's own range; a talking take longer than 15 s must be split

limits.price: UNCONFIRMED, USD, maker's direct price: a 5 s clip with no video input 0.35 at 480p (about 0.07 per second), 0.76 at 720p, 1.87 at 1080p; fast 0.28 at 480p. Billed in tokens = (input video seconds + output seconds) x width x height x frame rate / 1024, so a reference video raises the cost. Read from a search summary of https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/ModelArk/1544106, which could not be opened directly. Higgsfield's credit price is not in the local catalogue (base_credits 0.0000).
limits.unconfirmed: (1) audio_clip_seconds (2 s minimum per clip), audio_clip_mb, audio_formats, image_formats and max_image_mb come from reseller pages, not the maker's own page; (2) max_references_total: the maker lists 0-9 images, 0-3 videos and 0-3 audio, one reseller caps all files at 12 together; (3) whether Higgsfield's 2.0 reference-to-video lets a first/last-frame role sit beside audio (the 2.5 door refuses it with a 422); (4) whether a supplied voice track is lip-synced word for word: the maker says audio passes on its timbre, melody and dialogue content, and its examples type the line in the prompt with the voice taken from Audio n.
limits.note: On the maker's API, a first_frame / last_frame role is its own task type (image-to-video); inside a reference task a picture called 'the first frame' in the words is followed approximately. Text + audio alone, or audio alone, is refused.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: The words: who is which file, Shot 1 / Shot 2 / Shot 3 in event order, look, constraints.
inputs.allowed: no stated limit; the guide warns a whole script as the prompt confuses the model
inputs.we_send: same builder as 2.5, with shots in place of second windows

inputs.name: image (first frame)
inputs.what: The approved start picture. As role first_frame it is an image-to-video task; inside a reference task it is 'Image 1' named as the opening frame.
inputs.allowed: role first_frame (strict) or reference_image named as the opening frame (approximate); crop it to the output size or use ratio adaptive, or frames stretch and jump

inputs.name: image (reference)
inputs.what: A face, body, product, room, logo or look reference, each bound by number and job.
inputs.allowed: 0 to 9 reference images; a headshot plus one full-body photo per person; never a multi-view sheet or a collage; 4 people at most for a stable count
inputs.we_send: none in the chain; the bench can add them to test

inputs.name: image (last frame)
inputs.allowed: role last_frame with first_frame (image-to-video task), or named in the words of a reference task
inputs.we_send: silent clips only, only when different from the first

inputs.name: video (reference)
inputs.what: Motion, camera, effect or style from a clip; or the clip to edit or extend.
inputs.allowed: 0 to 3 videos, 15 s together; with or without their own sound
inputs.we_send: the swipe's blurred clips, up to 3, 15 s together, 'camera movement only'
inputs.use: yes where the swipe's movement is the point

inputs.name: audio (reference)
inputs.what: A voice timbre, music or rhythm; 'Character says: {line}, voice references Audio n'. Needs at least one picture or video beside it.
inputs.allowed: 0 to 3 clips, 15 s together; mp3 or wav, 15 MB each (UNCONFIRMED, reseller)
inputs.we_send: the line's locked read, one clip, bound as the speaker's voice; a read over 15 s cannot go in whole
inputs.use: test until word-for-word lip sync to a supplied read is proven

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.allowed: 480p, 720p, 1080p, 4k (10-bit H.265) on standard; 480p or 720p on fast and mini

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.allowed: 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 or adaptive (a fixed list, not 2.5's free 0.4 to 2.5 range)

inputs.name: generate_audio
inputs.what: Whether the clip carries sound made in the same pass (speech, effects, music).
inputs.allowed: true or false (default true on the maker's API)
inputs.we_send: true on talking clips, false on silent

inputs.name: return_last_frame
inputs.what: Hands back the clip's last frame, to start the next clip from it.

structure.rule: Name every file as type + number in upload order ('Image 1', 'Video 2', 'Audio 1'), counted within its own type; never by asset ID. Put the file that must be followed most precisely first.
Define each subject once by 2 to 3 stable features ('the woman in the red dress in Image 1 as Subject 1') and use that same label, or 'name@Image 1', every time it appears.
Order: subject + action details + scene + light and colour + camera move + style + image quality + constraints.
structure.ours: the summary block, then the shots, then constants

structure.rule: Write a storyboard as Shot 1 / Shot 2 / Shot 3 in event order (camera, action and expression, position, sound). Do not pin seconds: 2.0's precise timing ('0-3 s') is unstable and forcing it breaks the clip. This differs from 2.5's whole-second windows.
structure.ours: the timeline written as shots when the model is 2.0

structure.rule: One camera move per shot, in standard terms ('slow push-in', 'fixed shot'); push, pull, pan and track together make the picture unstable.
structure.ours: CAMERA phrases from the shot's camera_move

structure.rule: Name the body part, range, speed and force ('slowly raise a hand'); prefer slow, small, continuous movements and say how one action flows into the next.
Replace an emotion word with what the body visibly does (sad: head lowered, shoulders trembling, eyes reddening).
structure.ours: the emotion label is not sent

structure.rule: Mark sound by bracket: music in ( ), sound effects in < >, dialogue in { }, on-screen subtitles in 【 】; a language other than Chinese or English is named before the line. Keep all dialogue in one language.
structure.ours: dialogue braces on lines the model must speak

structure.rule: To use a voice: 'Character says: {line}, voice timbre references Audio n'; to place a sound: its timing + 'Audio n'. Describe the voice too ('the low, warm male voice of Audio 1') and keep the line's tone close to the reference.
structure.ours: Audio 1 bound as the speaker's voice

structure.rule: End with short constraints: 'keep it subtitle-free', 'do not generate a logo', 'do not generate a watermark', and, with several people, 'no duplicate characters'.
Use 4 to 5 files, not the full limit: 1 to 2 character pictures + 1 scene picture + 1 camera video + 1 audio clip. Too many files blur which one matters.
structure.ours: one picture, one voice, one clip

structure.rule: To edit or extend, call it 'Video n' directly ('Extend Video 1 backward', 'strictly edit Video 1'), never 'reference Video n', which turns it into a reference task; name what stays unchanged.
structure.ours: not used by the chain yet

avoid.text: Exact timestamps per shot ('0-3 seconds'): 2.0 follows them unreliably and the clip breaks.
Multi-view or three-view character sheets and mixed collages: read as several people, causing face drift and twins. Use a separate headshot and one full-body photo.
A photo or video of a real human face that is not the account's own model output, a preset character or an authorized asset: refused at input moderation.
Abstract emotion words ('very sad', 'extremely angry'): show the body instead.
Sprints, big jumps, violent rolls: high-burst actions are unstable.
Push, pull, pan and track in the same shot.
More than 4 referenced people in one clip: wrong head count and duplicates. Group them into pictures of 4 or fewer first.
References carrying words you do not want: they raise the chance of burnt-in subtitles. Portrait clips get subtitles more often than landscape; no prompt removes them 100%.
Mixing languages in the dialogue (proper nouns aside).
Text + audio only, or audio only: refused; an audio file needs a picture or video beside it.
Pasting the whole script as the prompt: redundant words confuse subjects; keep only what this clip shows.
Extending a model-made clip again and again: quality degrades with each pass, faces blotch. A narrated clip can also click at its end: fade the last audio out in the edit.

history.said: we are also going to do this for seedance too so we always get the best quality image and image to video

history.about: 2.0 sheet filled from the maker's 2.0 tutorial and prompt guide so the chain can prompt 2.0 as precisely as 2.5; draft until approved
